title: The differential sheaf of a group scheme is pulled back from the identity
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a group scheme over $K$ [def-sc-group-scheme], with structure morphism $f:G\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and identity $e:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$. For the relative differential sheaf $\Omega^1_{G/K}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] there is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_G$-modules $$\Omega^1_{G/K}\cong f^*e^*\Omega^1_{G/K},$$ where both pullbacks are ordinary module pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. No finite-type, smoothness, reducedness, commutativity, or restriction on the characteristic is assumed.

source.place: Tag 047I, label lemma-group-scheme-module-differentials, the canonical isomorphism Omega_{G/S} = f^*e^*Omega_{G/S}, specialized to S = Spec K.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $P=G\times_SG$, with projections $p_0,p_1$, and write $m$ and $i$ for multiplication and inverse. Since $m$ and $i$ are morphisms over $S$, both pairs below have equal composites to $S$. The morphisms $\tau=(m,p_1):P\to P$ and $\sigma=(m\circ(p_0,i\circ p_1),p_1):P\to P$ are defined by the fibre-product universal property. The first coordinates of $\sigma\tau$ and $\tau\sigma$ on a test scheme are $(gh)h^{-1}=g$ and $(gh^{-1})h=g$, respectively, by associativity, inverse and unit laws; their second coordinates are $h$. These identities are identities of morphisms by the group diagrams and the product universal property. Thus $\sigma\tau=\tau\sigma=\mathrm{id}_P$, and $p_1\tau=p_1\sigma=p_1$. No commutativity is used.

source.place: Tag 047I, label lemma-group-scheme-module-differentials, proof (shearing map and pullback along (e f, id))

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary cartesian base-change clause of [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] to $G\xrightarrow f S$ and the base morphism $G\xrightarrow f S$. Regard $P$ as a scheme over the second $G$ via $p_1$. With $\Omega=\Omega^1_{G/S}$ and $D=\Omega^1_{P/G}$ this gives the canonical isomorphism $c:p_0^*\Omega\xrightarrow\sim D$. Its local rule is $1\otimes da\mapsto d(p_0^\sharp a)$. The theorem applies without finite type, flatness, or smoothness.

source.place: Tag 01V0, label lemma-base-change-differentials; application in groupoids.tex Tag 047I

proof.text: The square with top map $\tau:P\to P$, both vertical maps $p_1:P\to G$, and bottom map $\mathrm{id}_G$ is cartesian. Indeed, for a compatible pair $a:T\to P$, $b:T\to G$ with $p_1a=b$, the lift $\sigma a$ satisfies $\tau\sigma a=a$ and $p_1\sigma a=p_1a=b$, since $p_1\sigma=p_1$. Any lift $u$ with $\tau u=a$ must equal $\sigma\tau u=\sigma a$. Thus this square satisfies the cartesian universal property, including uniqueness. In [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] take $X=P$, $S=S'=G$, $f=p_1$, $g=\mathrm{id}_G$, $p=\tau$, and $f'=p_1$. The just-proved universal property identifies this square with the chosen fibre-product square, so that theorem applies to it. We get the canonical differential isomorphism $c_\tau:\tau^*D\xrightarrow\sim D$, locally $1\otimes dz\mapsto d(\tau^\sharp z)$. This obtains invariance under the shearing automorphism directly from the same base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 047I, label lemma-group-scheme-module-differentials, proof (shearing map and pullback along (e f, id))

proof.text: Ordinary pullback is a functor and has the composition comparison in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Pulling $c$ back along $\tau$ and composing gives the isomorphism $\tau^*p_0^*\Omega\xrightarrow{\tau^*c}\tau^*D\xrightarrow{c_\tau}D\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}p_0^*\Omega$. Since $p_0\tau=m$, its source is canonically $m^*\Omega$. Denote the resulting isomorphism $a:m^*\Omega\xrightarrow\sim p_0^*\Omega$. Every arrow here is specified, so no choice of a trivialization or of a basis enters.

source.place: Tag 047I, label lemma-group-scheme-module-differentials, proof (shearing map and pullback along (e f, id))

proof.text: Let $s=(e\circ f,\mathrm{id}_G):G\to P$. This pair is compatible over $S$ since $f e=\mathrm{id}_S$. The left unit diagram gives $m s=\mathrm{id}_G$, and $p_0s=e f$. Apply $s^*$ to $a$ and the identity/composition comparisons of [def-pc-module-pullback]: $\Omega\cong s^*m^*\Omega\xrightarrow{s^*a}s^*p_0^*\Omega\cong(e f)^*\Omega\cong f^*e^*\Omega$. This is the required canonical $\mathcal O_G$-linear isomorphism. Only the group diagrams, product universal property and ordinary pullback were used; the argument imposes none of the finiteness, smoothness, reducedness, commutativity or characteristic restrictions excluded by the statement.
